price_gap.label: Kalshi cheaper than Polymarket
price_gap.why: Kalshi's ask is below Polymarket's price after the fee: two markets disagree, take the cheaper one.

futures.label: Tournament winner (draw sim)
futures.why: Draw-simulation title odds beat Kalshi's winner price; the one Kalshi market where the model was as sharp as the market (from the QF on).

line_shop.label: Sportsbook beats Pinnacle
line_shop.why: A US sportsbook pays more than Pinnacle's fair line: the approach that tested +1.4% to +3.1% per bet across sports.

pinnacle_gap.label: Kalshi cheaper than Pinnacle
pinnacle_gap.why: Kalshi's ask is below Pinnacle's no-vig price (the sharpest tennis book) after the fee.

tired_fav.label: Tired favourite vs fresh underdog
tired_fav.why: Favourite played 200+ min in the last 3 days, underdog under 90: the market over-marks the favourite down for fatigue (backtest +17% then +14% on 95 Kalshi matches, small sample). Re-checked on 15 years of bookmaker odds (10-day minutes version): +1.4% / +3.7% at Pinnacle and +3.3% / +6.1% at the best price, 2010-17 / 2018-24.

hot_dog_fade.label: Fade the hot underdog (paper)
hot_dog_fade.why: Back the favourite when the underdog is in hotter form (results beyond rating, 45 days, gap >= 0.10). On 27k matches with Pinnacle closing odds (2010-24) the favourite won 1-2 pts more than priced when the dog was hotter: +1.7% / +2.6% at the best book price in both halves, about 0% at Pinnacle; on Kalshi +0.7% / -0.1% after the fee. Paper until the live record shows it beats the fee.

veteran_fav.label: Veteran favourite (32+)
veteran_fav.why: Favourites aged 32+ won about 4 pts more than Kalshi priced, in both halves of 8,000 matches: +3.7% then +3.4% ROI at the real ask after the fee (about 330 bets each). Small stakes until the live record confirms it; skipped when the match is flagged stay-away.

lock.label: Lock (85%+ favourite, model agrees, no flags)
lock.why: Big favourites the market prices at 85%+, our model agrees within 10 pts, and no risk flags (no recent retirement, not 4+ matches in 7 days, not back from a long layoff). On 8,000 Kalshi matches they won 93.2% then 93.7% (priced 90.8%) and returned +1.4% then +2.0% at the real ask after the fee; at 90%+ they won 95-96%. Not certain: expect about 1 loss in 15. Skipped above 95c, where one loss wipes out ~20 wins. Also needs model confidence that isn't low: low-confidence locks won only 90-93% (break-even), confident ones 94-95% (+3.7% / +4.8%).

itf_big_gap.label: ITF: model rates the underdog 30+ pts higher (paper)
itf_big_gap.why: On 6,900 Kalshi ITF matches, when our model rated the market favourite 30+ pts lower than its price, the favourite won ~71% vs ~76-77% priced in both halves; backing the underdog returned +15% and +14% but with very wide error bars (about 400 bets). Paper-tracked until the live record confirms it. Smaller gaps (20 pts, or close matches where the model picks the underdog) flipped between halves.

itf_early.label: ITF early line (paper)
itf_early.why: On 6,800 Kalshi ITF matches the price moved toward our model after the open more often than away (51-53% vs 36-39%, both halves), so our ratings lead the ITF market a little. Betting our raw model at the open lost (spread + fee), but a 13% model / 90% market blend with a 6%+ edge at the early ask was positive out of sample (+4.8%, positive closing-line value) on only ~70 bets. Paper-tracked; the ledger and CLV will show whether it holds.

dog_value.label: Underdog value (model likes a cheap underdog)
dog_value.why: Underdogs priced 15-30c that our retuned model rates 10+ pts higher (20+ in ITF). On 8,100 tour/Challenger Kalshi matches they won 28% vs 23-24% priced: +15.3% then +11.1% at the real ask after the fee (all 15-30c underdogs: +0.9% / -9.3%). ITF: +3.2% / +3.1% (all ITF 15-30c dogs: -10% / -13%). They still lose ~3 times in 4, so stakes are small.
